generic_domain.justification: N-body simulations is a broader concept that includes n-body dynamics prediction as a specific application. N-body simulations involve computing the motion of multiple bodies interacting with each other, often under gravitational forces or other physical interactions. This field encompasses various methods and applications such as predicting planetary motions, stellar cluster evolution, and even particle physics phenomena. On the other hand, n-body dynamics prediction refers to the forecasting aspect within these simulations, focusing specifically on calculating how these bodies will move over time based on their initial conditions and mutual interactions. Therefore, while both domains are closely related and overlapping, 'N-body simulations' serves as a more comprehensive category that includes not only the predictions but also the computational frameworks, algorithms, data analysis methods, and various other aspects inherent to simulating n-body systems.
